events.title: Birth of Napoleon Bonaparte
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte was born in Ajaccio, Corsica. He rose through the ranks of the French military during the Revolution, became First Consul in 1799, and crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.
events.significance: Napoleon reshaped European politics, law, and warfare. His Napoleonic Code influenced legal systems worldwide, and his conquests redrew the map of Europe.

events.title: Opening of the Panama Canal
events.description: The Panama Canal officially opened to commercial traffic when the SS Ancon made the first full transit through the waterway connecting the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
events.significance: The canal dramatically shortened maritime travel between oceans, transformed global trade and naval strategy, and stands as one of the greatest engineering achievements of the early 20th century.

events.title: Japan Announces Surrender in World War II
events.description: Emperor Hirohito broadcast the Imperial Rescript on the Termination of the War, announcing Japan's acceptance of the Allied terms of surrender. The day is commemorated as V-J Day and as Liberation Day in Korea.
events.significance: The announcement effectively ended World War II, and the end of Japanese rule led to the liberation of Korea and other occupied territories, ushering in the postwar era.

events.title: Independence of India
events.description: India became independent from British rule at midnight, with Jawaharlal Nehru becoming the first Prime Minister. The same period saw the partition of British India into India and Pakistan.
events.significance: The end of British colonial rule in South Asia was a landmark in the decolonization movement, though partition caused mass displacement and violence affecting millions.

events.title: Woodstock Music Festival Begins
events.description: The Woodstock Music and Art Fair opened in Bethel, New York, drawing roughly 400,000 attendees over three days with performances by Jimi Hendrix, Janis Joplin, The Who, and many others.
events.significance: Woodstock became a defining moment of the 1960s counterculture and a lasting symbol of music, peace, and community.
